source_lines.51: 1.1 **Exact input.** Let V be a compact smooth d-dimensional bordism, with fixed horizontal incoming/outgoing faces and a fixed vertical product collar, on which the slicing function is t. Suppose a smooth one-parameter family (F_s,X_s), constant near the parameter endpoints, is supplied with the following proved properties. Each X_s is descending for F_s, is the fixed vertical product field near the protected collar, has the supplied smooth hyperbolic descending models at regular critical points, and is the exact negative cubic gradient on protected fold charts. No normalization of every regular eigenvalue is assumed. There are finitely many function events and finitely many transverse isolated same-index connecting-orbit events. No orbit joins a critical point of smaller index to one of larger index. Away from births the stable/unstable sections are smooth in the parameter. The actual compactness theorem for trajectories, including the fold endpoint sections, is part of the input. Near every birth the newborn critical points have no same-index connecting orbit to any other critical point. Their small birth block and the retained critical charts may be chosen uniformly. No slice-by-slice transversality of positive-index-drop trajectories is required. The proposed output is a smooth family g_s with the same critical points and indices, the same cubic births, X_s descending for g_s, and all critical values ordered by index. All boundary heights and protected collars are unchanged. Same-index heights may coincide at isolated crossings. Its full relative handle presentation is index grouped. Its actual equal-index trajectory events are unchanged because X_s is unchanged. The field theorem is used precisely through [F1]. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, construct]

Choose outer regular levels a<b containing just these two critical points. Their stable and unstable trajectory pieces in this slab, closed by their intersections with the outer levels, are compact and disjoint. Indeed the supplied broken-trajectory compactness permits a limit outside the indicated piece only by a broken orbit through the other critical point, which would give the excluded connection. The pieces stay away from the vertical collar, since the product trajectories there cannot approach an interior critical point. These separation properties persist on a smaller parameter neighborhood: a contrary sequence has a broken limit giving the same forbidden connection. Smooth dependence of the field and the Morse sections then applies uniformly. There is a smooth orbit-constant β_s on this slab, equal to one near the P trajectory piece and zero near the Q trajectory piece and the vertical collar. Here are the extension details. On the lower regular face choose a bump equal to one on a neighborhood of the compact P unstable exit section and zero near the Q unstable exit section and the boundary. The sections are disjoint compact sets, so the bump can be chosen uniformly for s near s₀; let it be one on one fixed open neighborhood containing every nearby P exit section. Extend by flow to every trajectory meeting the lower face. Set the extension one on trajectories ending at P and zero on those ending at Q. Near either regular critical trajectory piece the resulting function is constant, without requiring an exact exponential chart. Indeed, if regular points approaching that piece had lower exits outside the chosen constant neighborhood, take convergent parameters and such points. The supplied uniform broken-trajectory compactness gives a limiting broken orbit through the corresponding critical point. The absence of a connection between P and Q, and strict descent excluding a return to the same critical height, force its last segment to leave that same critical point through its unstable exit section. This contradicts the choice of exits outside an open neighborhood of the entire compact exit section. The same argument applies to points on the stable sheet and uniformly for nearby parameters, since the exit neighborhoods were chosen to contain every nearby compact section. Thus the extension is identically one, respectively zero, on a full neighborhood of each critical trajectory piece. There is therefore no nonsmooth quotient at the limiting sheet. On its remaining domain the exit time and exit point are smooth by the implicit function theorem for a regular level. This proves smoothness jointly in s and space. A minimum with no unstable exit has an open attracting set on which the value is set constantly one or zero. Its possible boundary inside the slab would limit to the other critical point; the excluded connection rules that out near the chosen trajectory piece. The same argument applied to the reversed field handles a maximum and an upper-face construction. The extension is zero near the vertical product trajectories because the lower bump is zero there, and the product flow has no critical endpoint there. Thus X_sβ_s=0 everywhere. A cutoff in the level coordinate may be used outside this outer slab; take it only where the height change below is already identity, so it contributes no derivative term. Choose a smooth increasing interval diffeomorphism φ_s of [a,b], identity near its endpoints and affine with positive slope near the P critical value, carrying that value to a desired position still inside (a,b). Define $G_s(u,z)=(1-z)u+z\phi_s(u),\qquad \widetilde F_s=G_s(F_s,\beta_s).$ Then ∂_uG_s>0, and $X_s\widetilde F_s=(\partial_uG_s)(F_s,\beta_s)X_sF_s<0$ off the original critical points. source_lines.44: 1.1 The left-module presentation reverses the algebra-bimodule $1$-morphism orientation: a module functor $\operatorname{Mod}^l(A)\to\operatorname{Mod}^l(B)$ is represented by a $B$-$A$ bimodule, while the algebra convention $A\to B$ uses $A$-$B$ bimodules. Thus the algebra presentation of this module $2$-category uses the $1$-morphism opposite of that algebra bicategory. Tensor multiplication on objects is unchanged. Under this passage the evaluation and coevaluation arrows exchange, and left and right dual roles exchange; both dual orientations have been constructed separately. Preserve the positive braided tensor algebra K=A⊗B. Let P=Mod^l_C(K). Define b(M,N)=M⊗N, with K-action `(l_M⊗l_N)(1_A⊗c_{B,M}⊗1_N)`. [F1, F2, given, algebra]
source_lines.46: 1.2 Naturality and the hexagons prove its action equation exactly as for the positive tensor-algebra multiplication. Define balance by `1_M⊗c_{N,X}^{-1}: MXN→MNX`; this is K-linear: expand c_{B,MX}, cancel the c_{B,X} against c_{N,X}^{-1} by naturality with l_N, and the remaining composite is the target K-action. The balance/unit equation is the braiding unit equation. For balance associativity on $MXYN$, both composites are the inverse braid taking $XYN$ to $NYX$: move $Y$ behind $N$ and then $X$ behind $NY$, or move $XY$ behind $N$ and then interchange $X,Y$ by $c_{Y,X}^{-1}$. The inverse hexagon expands both to the same three inverse crossings. Compatibility with the outer right action is the other inverse hexagon. Hence b is a balanced right-module functor. It is exact and bilinear because all tensor functors in a fusion category are exact. [F1, F2, given, algebra]
source_lines.48: 1.3 Here is a proof of universality which also specifies its action on transformations. A right K-object d in a finite semisimple right C-module category D is an object equipped with r:d⊙K→d satisfying the algebra action equations. It determines a module functor H_d:P→D by `H_d(L)=d⊙_K L`. [F1, F2, given, algebra]
source_lines.50: 1.4 Construct $H_d(L)$ as the image of the separability idempotent `(r⊙l_L)(1_d⊙e_K⊙1_L)` on d⊙L. Its image exists because D is finite semisimple. The usual centrality and unit equations for e_K show this image corepresents K-balanced maps, just as for the ordinary bimodule supplier: the idempotent is fixed by every balanced map; conversely its projection is balanced. No new coequalizer existence theorem is being assumed. This construction is functorial in L and K-linear maps d→d'. [F1, F2, given, algebra]
source_lines.52: 1.5 Conversely any module functor H:P→D is canonically H_d with d=H(K). Its right action is H(m_K):H(K⊗K)≅H(K)⊙K→H(K). On free modules K⊗X, its module constraint gives H(K⊗X)≅d⊙X. Every K-module L is a retract of K⊗L: the action is the retraction and the section is `(1_K⊗l_L)(e_K⊗1_L)`. This section is K-linear by centrality, and its action composite is 1_L. Hence the free-module comparison extends uniquely to all retracts. To check naturality it suffices to check free maps. Such a map K⊗X→K⊗Y is uniquely `(m_K⊗1_Y)(1_K⊗f)` for f:X→K⊗Y obtained by inserting η_K; H and H_d agree on this expression by the definition of r. Transformations agree precisely when their value at K is K-linear. This proves an equivalence of categories, including transformations, between module functors P→D and right K-objects in D. For a balanced module functor F:Mod^l(A)×Mod^l(B)→D, put d=F(A,B). Denote its outer constraint by `δ:F(M,NX)→F(M,N)⊙X` and its balance by β. Put `θ=δβ:F(MX,N)→F(M,N)⊙X`. Define `r_A=F(m_A,1_B) θ_{A,A,B}^{-1}:d⊙A→d`, `r_B=F(1_A,m_B) δ_{A,B,B}^{-1}:d⊙B→d`. [F1, F2, given, algebra]
source_lines.54: 1.6 Naturality with the algebra multiplications proves their associative/unital action equations. Expanding the balance/outer compatibility square gives the precise exchange equation `r_A(r_B⊙1_A)=r_B(r_A⊙1_B)(1_d⊙c_{B,A}):d⊙B⊙A→d`. [F1, F2, given, algebra]
source_lines.56: 1.7 For an explicit verification, replace θ by δβ, move each multiplication through δ by its naturality, and through β by naturality in its module arguments. The residual two routes move the free B slot past the free A slot. The balance-associativity equation for the chosen inverse left conversion replaces that move by c_{B,A}; its inverse crossing is cancelled by the inverse in θ^-1. The remaining maps are F(m_A,m_B) on both routes. Thus `r=r_B(r_A⊙1_B)` is a right K-action: its iterated action on dABAB first moves the middle B past A by c_{B,A}, then uses the two individual action equations, exactly giving r(1_d⊙m_K). This proves the action equation without assuming ordinary commuting actions. [F1, F2, given, algebra]
source_lines.58: 1.8 The functor H_d b is canonically equivalent to F. On free pairs first use δ to identify $F(AX,BY)$ with $F(AX,B)\odot Y$, and then θ on the first factor, to obtain `F(A⊗X,B⊗Y)≅d⊙X⊙Y`. Meanwhile the positive crossing `1_A⊗c_{B,X}⊗1_Y` is a K-linear isomorphism `K⊗X⊗Y→b(A⊗X,B⊗Y)`. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

source_lines.41: 1.1 Let D=C⊠C, whose objects needed here are pairs, with componentwise tensor. Define `T(U,V)=U⊗V` and strong tensorator `t_{(U,V),(U',V')}=1_U⊗c_{V,U'}⊗1_{V'} : UVU'V'→UU'VV'`. [F1, F2, given, algebra]
source_lines.43: 1.2 The tensorator pentagon compares three such pairs. Expanding crossings past products by the two hexagons leaves crossings V1 past U2,U3 and V2 past U3; the two crossings on disjoint slots commute. Thus the two composites coincide. Unit coherence follows from the braiding unit equation. This proves T strong monoidal without a strictification theorem: insert the given associations and its pentagon throughout. [F1, F2, given, algebra]
source_lines.45: 1.3 For R=(A,B), put `mu=(m_A,m_B)`, `s=(sigma_A,sigma_B)`. In D, `mu s=id` and `s mu=(mu⊗id)(id⊗s)=(id⊗mu)(s⊗id)`, componentwise. Put `K=T(R)`, `m=T(mu)t`, `sigma=t^{-1}T(s)`. Naturality of t and its just-proved coherence transport the THREE equations to `m sigma=id_K`, `sigma m=(m⊗id_K)(id_K⊗sigma)`, `sigma m=(id_K⊗m)(sigma⊗id_K)`. [F1, F2, given, algebra]
source_lines.47: 2.1 For clarity the first left-linearity transport starts with `t^{-1} T(s mu)t`; replace `s mu` by `(mu⊗id)(id⊗s)`, use naturality to move T(s) to the last two inputs, and use the tensorator pentagon to replace the two intervening tensorators by `(t⊗id)(id⊗t^{-1})`. This is exactly `(T(mu)t⊗id)(id⊗t^{-1}T(s))`. The right-linearity calculation replaces `s mu` by `(id⊗mu)(s⊗id)` and gives `(id⊗T(mu)t)(t^{-1}T(s)⊗id)` in the same way. These are both linearity composites, not merely a multiplication/section cancellation. Expanding t gives exactly the candidate `sigma=(1_A⊗c_{B,A}^{-1}⊗1_B)(sigma_A⊗sigma_B)`. [F1, F2, given, algebra] ∎
